title: Breathing-Qwen + Luotain: residue chooses the next computation
summary: Three same-day projects expose the same narrower pattern from different domains: contradictory or incomplete evidence should not be forced into the current answer; keep the mismatch or residue explicit and let it decide which computation to try next. The two Qwen repositories independently find that simple counterfactual re-query or leave-one-clue-out search survives while the more elaborate breathing and trust mechanisms tested so far do not beat simpler controls. Luotain applies a parallel probe-first discipline to equational theories: cheap finite tables eliminate almost all false implications, and only the unresolved residue is handed to a theorem prover. This pass records convergence, not code ancestry.

nodes.claim: Tests whether a frozen Qwen3-8B can recover from one contradictory clue by diagnosing cue-specific residue and then re-querying the intact joint model without retraining, stochastic decoding, or rewriting the prompt history.
nodes.survived: On the frozen 32-item Gate 1B development set, residue-guided intact re-query reaches 93.75% corrupt accuracy versus 75.0% for native Qwen and 59.375% for random cue removal, with 6 native-error recoveries, 0 new native errors, and 30/32 suspicious-cue localization accuracy (93.75%). Clean accuracy remains 90.625%. The surviving recipe is narrower than the original breathing story: decompose to diagnose, identify one suspicious cue, then ask the intact joint model again without that cue dominating the decision.
nodes.killed: Gate 0 and Gate 1-Q4 failed their frozen criteria; external candidate-score temperature/beta breathing did no useful selection work in Gate 1-Q4, and true internal attention-temperature breathing remains untested. Gate 1C is frozen on a new 128-item holdout but is not run, so the Gate 1B development result is not independent confirmation and must not be promoted to a held-out claim yet.

nodes.claim: Independently tests corrupted-clue retrieval with text-level breathing, attention-trust variants, leave-one-clue-out search and residue-guided search, using predeclared comparisons against simpler controls.
nodes.survived: Across the 60-item benchmark, plain one-shot corrupted retrieval is 52%, while the simple leave-one-clue-out dropout control with checking reaches 75%. More elaborate runs keep returning to that same robust boundary: remove one clue, compare the counterfactual answers, and use checking to find which clue is poisoning the joint answer. That simple counterfactual search is the strongest surviving result.
nodes.killed: The attention trust loop did not beat the simple dropout control under the predeclared rule, so the mechanistic breathing claim was killed. A later residue_search arm reached 72% on the false-clue condition versus 75% for dropout; it was substantially cheaper but did not beat the accuracy control. The repository name is historical: these experiments do not establish globally oscillating internal attention temperature.

nodes.claim: Maps equational theories by using small multiplication tables as explicit probes, treating a counterexample table as a certificate of non-implication and escalating only the undecided residue to Vampire and sampled Lean checking.
nodes.survived: On the published four-multiplication map, ten two-element tables alone kill 90.66% of false implications; all probe families together kill 99.53% (13,789,681 false edges) while killing zero of 8,173,585 true implications. On the 57,882 five-multiplication laws, the placement finds at least 9,086 new equivalence classes. For 150 sampled new laws against all 1,415 old classes, probes decide 98.6% of 424,500 edges and probes plus Vampire settle 99.75%.
nodes.killed: The five-multiplication layer is not fully settled: 1,278 laws remain in the placement residue, and 1,054 cross-layer edges remain open in the sampled exhaustive edge experiment. The full implication graph among all five-multiplication laws was not computed. Lean re-checks a random sample rather than every claim; the remainder rests on the tested evaluator and Vampire, so Luotain does not claim a fully Lean-certified new map.

edges.why: Both freeze Qwen3-8B and ask how contradictory evidence can change retrieval without changing model weights. AdaptiveObserverCache intervenes on a persistent reader/attention state over fixed memory; Breathing-Qwen tested a different route and narrowed the surviving mechanism to residue-guided diagnosis plus intact counterfactual re-query. This is conceptual and experimental convergence, not code ancestry.

The two independently implemented corrupted-cue studies land on the same measured boundary: simple counterfactual cue removal or re-query survives, while the tested breathing and trust-loop mechanisms do not beat simpler controls. The edge records convergence of results and does not assert a fork or code inheritance.

ReadWrite treats designed interventions as what makes otherwise hidden structure observable. Luotain turns finite magmas into explicit probes of law space, uses counterexamples as certificates, and spends theorem-prover compute only on what those probes cannot separate. The relationship is methodological convergence, not implementation ancestry.

motifs.title: Residue routes the next computation
motifs.description: Across contradictory-cue retrieval and law-space probing, the useful repeat is not to overwrite the object when a candidate fails. Preserve what remains unexplained, then spend the next computation where that residue points: re-query without a suspicious clue, or invoke a theorem prover only on finite-probe residue. The same-day measurements also impose a boundary: residue-directed routing survived, while the tested breathing and trust mechanisms did not establish an additional advantage.
